summary: eth-keystore-utils ships install-time reverse shell to hardcoded C2
details: The gem declares ext/req_throttle_mini/extconf.rb as a native extension but ships no C/C++ sources — the directory contains only extconf.rb ending in a bare `create_makefile('eth_keystore_utils_native')`, so the extension listing exists solely to force extconf.rb to run during `gem install`. extconf.rb base64-decodes an embedded Ruby payload and evaluates it inside a double-forked, detached, sleep-delayed child. The decoded payload opens a TCP connection to the hardcoded bare-IP C2 at 45.138.12.177:8090 and bridges it bidirectionally to /bin/sh via IO.popen and IO.copy_stream, giving the operator of that host an interactive shell on the installer's machine. Execution is gated by anti-analysis checks that look for CI environment variables, ephemeral/generated hostnames and usernames, sandbox-like cwd paths, short machine uptime (<1800s), and the presence of developer artifacts (~/.ssh, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.gem/credentials) so the backdoor only fires on real developer workstations. The package name impersonates Ethereum keystore tooling to attract wallet-adjacent targets.
